quoted.text: $MRVL held a webcast today on its acquisition of Lumentum. On slide 13 they show an NPO module with a DSP in it (pictured below) Our channel checks indicate that Marvell is working on a TX-only DSP for NPO. The transmit side is retimed and the receive side stays linear, so it is not a fully retimed DSP. That adds about 30 to 35 ns of latency, against roughly 90 ns for a fully retimed DSP. The point of NPO was to sit close enough to the ASIC to go without a DSP. The electrical path from the ASIC to the optics was meant to be short enough to skip the DSP. It looks like the electrical losses on the host side and the need for stable scale-up links are enough to warrant a retimer on the transmit side after all. It is still early, but adding a DSP would reduce NPO’s power and latency advantages over pluggables. It would also give Marvell another DSP socket inside a design that was originally intended to not work with one.
